question: Which of the following is the best-known metabolic function of the lung

options.opd: Metabolism of basic drugs by cytochrome P–450 system

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Lung" -> "presence of ACE" -> "conversion of angiotensin-I to angiotensin-II" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Lung" -> "cytochrome P-450 system" -> "metabolism of basic drugs" -> "possible" -> 50%
analysis: The lung is known for several metabolic functions, but the most prominent and well-documented is the conversion of angiotensin-I to angiotensin-II. This process is facilitated by the angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE), which is abundantly present in the pulmonary endothelium. While the lung does participate in the inactivation of serotonin and bradykinin, these functions are not as widely recognized or emphasized in medical literature as the conversion of angiotensin-I to angiotensin-II. The metabolism of basic drugs by the cytochrome P-450 system is primarily associated with the liver, not the lung. Therefore, based on standard medical knowledge and consensus, the conversion of angiotensin-I to angiotensin-II is the best-known metabolic function of the lung.
